items.reason: The sync branch returns a raw fetch Response incompatible with the provider-specific shapes expected by its callers.
Google persists the safeParse wrapper instead of its data, corrupting the stored credential shape.
The computed schema keys are literal names rather than wildcard validators, so synced expiry and other token fields are not preserved.
Bigin passes the credential ID as the user ID, causing sync requests to identify the wrong user.
The Salesforce credential update references prisma without importing or declaring it.
The comment includes the unconditional Salesforce refresh and database write on every service construction, even with a valid token. It additionally mentions the stale connection credentials.
The computed Zod keys do not implement dynamic property matching or preserve arbitrary expiry fields, matching the existing schema problem.
Google saves the safeParse result wrapper as the credential key instead of saving its data.
The raw fetch Response returned in sync mode violates the response contracts expected by Google, HubSpot, and Zoho callers.
Bigin supplies credentialId where refreshOAuthTokens expects the owner's userId.
Persisting the safeParse wrapper nests Google's token fields under data and breaks subsequent credential parsing.
Sync returns an undecoded fetch Response while several consumers expect parsed provider-specific token objects.
The comment identifies the same computed-key schema defect that strips expiry and other token fields. It also describes the downstream refresh-token placeholder consequence.
Google persists the parser's result wrapper rather than the token payload in its data field.
The sync branch returns a fetch Response instead of the SDK/Axios or token-object shapes its consumers require.
Bigin passes a credential row ID as calcomUserId rather than passing the nullable credential owner's user ID.
The Google refresh path stores the safeParse envelope instead of the credentials themselves.
Literal computed schema keys fail to retain normal expiry and other token properties in sync responses.
Returning a raw fetch Response in sync mode breaks callers expecting provider-specific parsed response shapes.
The Bigin caller serializes credential.id as calcomUserId because it passes the wrong identifier to refreshOAuthTokens.
The webhook compares its shared secret using ordinary string inequality instead of a constant-time comparison.
